newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish labour minister Baczkowski dies.
newsitem.headline: Polish labour minister Baczkowski dies.

text.p: Poland's Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski, a rare veteran of the pre-1989 Solidarity movement in a government dominated by ex-communists, died on Thursday at the age of 41, PAP news agency reported.
The agency quoted government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska as announcing his death but did not give its cause.

Baczkowski, an academic specialising in labour law, advised Solidarity after it emerged as the Soviet bloc's first free trade union in 1980 and was interned when Communist leader Wojciech Jaruzelski declared martial law to crush the union in 1981.

He took a senior post in the labour and social policy ministry after the 1989 fall of communism and was appointed a non-party minister early this year in the coalition cabinet, now led by ex-communists and Peasant party members.
He was also appointed to a special post responsible for evolving a new social security system -- one of the thorniest and most crucial challenges facing the government.

Baczkowski had to deal with such complex issues as finding jobs for workers from the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, where Solidarity was born, controlling nationwide unemployment benefit fraud, and meeting backlogs in pensions payments.
